 Vehicle Recalls Cover Brake, Steering and Air Bag Issues
 Free Press Publisher 
 November 10, 2026 
 Lifestyle and Travel News 
 Five National Highway Traffic Safety Administration recalls affect vehicles manufactured by Ford, General Motors, Mack Trucks and Hyundai.
 Ford Motor Company’s recall 26V691 covers 2025–2027 Lincoln Navigator vehicles because the front passenger seat may move unexpectedly.
 General Motors’ recall 26V717 concerns a loss of braking and affects these models:
 2025–2026 Cadillac Celestiq 
 2023–2027 Cadillac Lyriq 
 2026–2027 Cadillac Vistiq 
 2024–2027 Chevrolet Blazer EV 
 A separate General Motors recall, 26V718 , covers 2025–2026 Chevrolet Express and GMC Savana vehicles for an improperly tightened steering gear assembly nut.
 Mack Trucks’ recall 26V719 affects 2024–2026 Mack MD Electric trucks because a hill start assist message is incorrectly enabled.
 Hyundai Motor America’s recall 26V728 covers 2019–2023 Hyundai Kona Electric and 2019–2022 Hyundai Veloster N vehicles. Air bags and seat belt pretensioners may not deploy in a crash.
 Owners can enter their license plate or vehicle identification number in NHTSA’s Recall Lookup Tool to check whether their vehicle is affected. Vehicles with an unrepaired recall can be repaired free of charge by scheduling an appointment with a local dealership.

 The Franklin County Free Press, established by Vicky Taylor in 2019, emerged as a beacon of local journalism for the residents of Franklin County. Under Vicky's leadership, it quickly became an essential source of news, particularly at a time when major newspaper publications were increasingly overlooking local coverage. 
On January 1, 2022, the torch was passed to Nathan Neil and his firm, Neil Publishing, LLC. Neil, a local entrepreneur with multiple thriving businesses in Chambersburg, shares Vicky's fervent commitment to both the community and the world of local journalism. 
Rooted in the heart of Franklin County and powered by its residents, the Franklin County Free Press continues to bridge the gap, ensuring that the local stories, events, and issues that matter most to the community remain in the spotlight.
